title: 2015 HMMT November General Problem 4
statement: Chords \(A B\) and \(C D\) of a circle are perpendicular and intersect at a point \(P\). If \(A P=6, B P=12\), and \(C D=22\), find the area of the circle.

solutions.text:
Answer: \(130 \pi\)
Let \(O\) be the center of the circle and let \(M\) be the midpoint of segment \(A B\) and let \(N\) be the midpoint of segment \(C D\). Since quadrilateral \(O M P N\) is a rectangle we have that \(O N=M P=A M-A P=3\) so

\[O C=\sqrt{O N^{2}+N C^{2}}=\sqrt{9+121}=\sqrt{130}\]

Hence the desired area is \(130 \pi\).
